mappings.note: Assigns a function (regulating enucleate sieve tubes) to one component inside a complex tissue, the phloem counterpart of the xylem-parenchyma item in part 2. Role outcome, not LO-1: no xylem/phloem comparison is made.
The stem asks outright which statement distinguishes xylem from phloem, so LO-1 leads; C3.2 because the property being contrasted is directionality of transport, a life process that competency names.

The false statement is a structural one (abundant intercellular matrix, which belongs to connective tissue), and the true pair is dense packing plus regulation of exchange - so structure first, role second. LO-1 is unavailable here: it does not list an epithelial/connective discrimination.

Picks the epithelial subtype whose flatness and single layer suit rapid diffusion - the structural property is the whole basis of the choice. Kept to one code; unlike the 3-mark version in part 1 the diffusion process itself does not have to be explained.

Three samples described purely by cell shape, layering and site, each to be matched to a function. This is the structure-to-function outcome applied three times; no tissue name even has to be produced, so LO-1 is not in play.

Every statement is a bare tissue-to-function pairing with no structural description given, and the false one misassigns a role (cuboidal as sensory). Role outcome, split from the neighbouring sample-table item, which supplies structure and withholds function.

Trimming a hedge and getting lateral shoots is an applied role question about intercalary meristem. LO-1 is cited here, unlike the other meristem-subtype items, because option D offers a permanent tissue as the growth source, forcing the meristematic/permanent discrimination.
The answer is what ciliated epithelium does for the respiratory tract - sweeping mucus and trapped particles clear - a role in the body rather than a structure-to-property derivation.

The reason offered is structural and false (no nuclei), so the student must supply the correct structural basis for the barrier function: continuous, densely packed cells. Structure-to-function throughout.

Asks for the defining architecture of connective tissue - sparse cells in an abundant extracellular matrix. Fit is partial: only structure is scored, and the frame has no structure-alone outcome, so C-4.2-LO-2 is used as the nearest.
The stem defines blood as a connective tissue by its liquid matrix and asks that matrix to be named, so what is scored is the structural composition of the tissue, not what blood does.
Attributes clotting to one formed element of blood - the role of a tissue component in the body. Split from the plasma item above, which is about blood's structural make-up.

Three lost functions are traced back to tendon, ligament and cartilage - role of tissues in animals. LO-5 rejected: the item stops at identifying the damaged tissue and asks nothing about recovery techniques or medical recommendations.
The stem sets up rigid support and then asks what the matrix is made of, so the calcium/phosphorus answer is the structural basis of that function. Composition-to-property, hence C-4.2-LO-2.
A four-way match of bone, cartilage, tendon and ligament to what each does. List-II is entirely functions, with no structural descriptors, so the role outcome carries it alone.

Role of ligaments in holding articulating bones, reached through an athlete's knee dislocation. C-5.3-LO-2 is cited here, and not on the clinical three-patient item, because this stem frames the tissue in terms of sporting activity - the split rule for that outcome throughout this chapter.
Plain attribution of force transmission to tendon, with no activity or injury framing, so it stays on the role outcome alone while the athlete item above also takes C-5.3-LO-2.

A negative-stem item about where cartilage does and does not occur, which is knowledge of the role it plays at each site (ear, nose tip, bone ends) versus a secretory lining. No structural reasoning is required.

A flexible tendril and a brittle woody branch have to be sorted into collenchyma and sclerenchyma from their mechanical behaviour - the discrimination in LO-1, read through wall structure. C-8.2-LO-3 rejected: the stress test yields no data to analyse, it only supplies the contrast.
Fibre shape, nuclei count and the false claim about striations are exactly the features that separate striated, smooth and cardiac muscle, the clause LO-1 names.

Every distractor is an action performed by a different muscle type (lifting, heartbeat, turning the head), so the muscle-type discrimination in LO-1 leads; C-4.2-LO-3 for attributing peristalsis to smooth muscle as a role in the body.

Tendon and ligament identified from what each connects on a joint model. Same outcome as the knee-diagram item in part 2, reached from attachment rather than from function; both are role-of-tissue, and neither has an activity framing that would pull in C-5.3-LO-2.

Ordering the reflex path requires knowing what each part of a neuron does - dendrites receive, axon conducts - which is structure-to-function; C-4.2-LO-3 for the role of nervous tissue in coordinating the response.
The stem explicitly asks how cardiac muscle differs from skeletal and smooth, and every option is a structural description. Straight onto the striated/smooth/cardiac clause of LO-1.

The false reason is a voluntary/involuntary claim, which is the muscle-type discrimination (LO-1); C-4.2-LO-3 for the assertion itself, which is about the lifelong role cardiac muscle performs. Split from the structure-only cardiac item above, which stays on LO-1 alone.
